[0] everyday_reading (E): In everyday writing, layout carries meaning: one value per line, '1,000' with a comma, '12.' as a number. To StdIn, any run of whitespace is one separator, a token is a maximal run of non-whitespace, and it must be written as a Java literal of the expected type.

[0] names_the_element (N): Input format is the contract for the text on standard input: whitespace-separated tokens, each one a literal of the type the program asks for next.
[1] states_the_rule (S): StdIn treats consecutive whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines) as one space. Whenever the program expects a value of a type, the next token must be a value of that type.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): For each token read, leading whitespace is skipped, then the maximal non-whitespace run is taken and parsed. At a terminal, characters reach the program only a whole line at a time, after <return>.
[1] output_prediction (OP): The input `  144\n\t233 ` gives readInt() 144, then 233. readDouble() on `5` gives 5.0. readInt() on `12.2` throws.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One token read consumes the leading whitespace and one token, and leaves the whitespace after it.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Every StdIn read applies these format rules. The type of the method called decides which tokens are legal.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): A token in the wrong format makes a read throw, so validation must check before reading (e.g. Scanner.hasNextDouble) or read a String and test it.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): A shared format convention lets independently produced data files feed a program. PlotFilter, for example, expects the first four numbers to be the bounding box.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Reformatting whitespace (spaces to newlines, extra blanks, tabs) keeps every read's result. Changing a token's form (5 to 5.0, or adding a comma) can break readInt.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The next token must be a literal of the requested type. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: Tokens like abc, 12.2, true or 1,000 when readInt() is called.
[2] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Whitespace-token format suits numeric data and single-word strings. When values contain spaces, or the line structure matters, use readLine.
Input format rules apply to every StdIn read.
